summary: EVIDENCE: exact divisor/Liouville sieve to 10^8 finds Pearson(D,λ)=0.000601504 on the 25,000,000 integers N≡1 mod 4, but P(D>0|λ=±1)=0.728037909 versus 0.662503349. On 818,702 primes p≤12,499,999 the two-form λ correlation for (4p+1,8p+1) is −0.000439720, while the D₁D₂-weighted moment is −0.052668737. Z1996 actually reports pooled slice-success rates, not this count correlation; the needed prime-restricted divisor-weighted Chowla statement is formulated in the memo.
not_done: No proof of weighted Chowla or growing-C uniformity; C=2 statistics use class 3 mod 4, not class 7 mod 8.
next: Separate count and positivity weights, with prime and residue conditioning, before using a Chowla input.

summary: PROVED relative to Treviño Corollary 2/Table 3: c₂(10)=1.5216, p≥10^20, all interval lengths; Theorem 2 alone has a length restriction. Explicit partial summation gives g(p)≤0.275log p+0.5loglog p+16.150725927, and elementary explicit divisor-sum bounds yield M_BM(p)≥3(log p)^2/(32π²) for every prime p≥10^1000. A numerical crossing is near 10^150.0553, but only the conservative threshold is claimed; the ES remainder is untouched.
not_done: No optimal threshold, prime census to p₁, or bound for R−M_BM.
next: Review the explicit harmonic-sum constants before using this threshold in a conditional theorem.

summary: CERTIFIED: the exact K1′ theta-quotient coefficients D⁻_t(tn+1)−D⁺_t(tn+1) were sieved for t=2..64, n=0..100000; signs change, including 3503 positives at t=5 and 1125 at the ES level t=16. At t=5,n=39, N=196 gives D⁻−D⁺=3−2=1, while n=0 gives −1. METAPLECTIC_ES §1 identifies the quotient but only establishes one-sided signs at special small levels; the numerical check rules out general sign-rigidity, not ES.
not_done: No new modular normalisation or QUE pointwise theorem.
next: Do not substitute theta-value equidistribution for positivity of a prescribed Fourier coefficient.

summary: PROVED algebra: with q=4C,N=qp+1 the (★) slice is 0∈{1}+∏_{ℓ^v||N}{1,ℓ,…,ℓ^v} in Z/q; this is an ET Type II subfamily, not literal ET Type I. Bourgain 2005 was located, and its subgroup theorem plus composite-modulus projection hypotheses were read in his full 2007 follow-up. At C≈p^θ, θ>0, the actual divisor-product set has size p^o(1), below q^ε; replacing it by a generated subgroup loses the bounded divisor exponents, as §(c3) warns.
not_done: The 2005 proof itself was not downloaded; its theorem is checked in the authors 2007 full text. No subgroup completion-to-divisor implication.
next: Any usable theorem must retain bounded prime exponents and force the specified target, not merely expand a generated subgroup.

summary: Read DFI pp.23–25 and found the actual Weil use in EXCEPTIONAL_MN4 §§2.6–2.7: normalized error exponent 2ρ+α−δ, with spectral first term 2ρ+(δ−α)/2. B7 mislabels the 3/8,11/48 estimate: it is DFI Theorem 2; combining Theorems 1–2 gives savings 1/48,1/20,1/10,1/4 for (M,N)=(X^μ,X), μ=1,.9,.8,.5. These are savings against trivial bilinear bounds, not interchangeable gains on the ES Weil remainder: the required independent weights are absent (f=4uC−1 and overline(4C)=u mod f).
not_done: No new separable dispersion identity or improved exceptional-set exponent.
next: An ES-specific factorisation of the coupled weights is required before any DFI exponent can be transferred.

summary: PROVED relative to Banaszczyk 1996: using cube/cross-polytope Gaussian transference gives L_min=O(k√log k)/Δ instead of k^(3/2)/Δ, reducing the original CONDITIONAL GRH+EQ and GRH+S cap exponents 13/2→6 and 9/2→4. Exact dual-minimum enumeration at q=237971,423883 improves finite sufficient caps 4385→3710 and 1205→775 using the existing all-dimension Euclidean constant. R–SD Theorem 1.5 needs every dual sublattice determinant, so supplies no better threshold from Δ alone; the 0.1275+o(1) improved Euclidean constant is not explicit at small k.
not_done: No explicit universal Gaussian-transference constant, full dual-sublattice determinant census, or proof of EQ/S; no ES consequence.
next: Review and incorporate the classical norm-aware bound into the conditional cap theorems, retaining their arithmetic hypotheses.

summary: Formulated a uniform relative Hardy–Littlewood lower/asymptotic count for admissible L_i(t)=a_it+b_i with coefficients≤T^(1+ε), including positivity, box size and singular-series conditions. GTZ has a second obstruction beyond coefficient size: its §1 Example 2 explicitly says every one-variable system with more than one form has infinite complexity, so even fixed coefficients are not covered. Bienvenu Theorem 1.3 (arXiv:1607.06625) genuinely allows polylogarithmic linear coefficients for finite-complexity multivariable systems; Brun–Titchmarsh is only an upper bound and Siegel–Walfisz only reaches logarithmic modulus powers.
not_done: No new uniform prime-tuples theorem or verified ES parametrisation satisfying it.
next: Check finite complexity before coefficient uniformity in any proposed primes-to-certificates map.

summary: KUDLA_ES explicitly says the degree identities are cited, not used, so pass1 covered was too broad. Using Kudla §5 formulas (5.3)–(5.5), explicit maximal orders and stack automorphism weights, I computed special 0-cycle degrees at d=1 in characteristics 3,7 for m≤1000: 200/334 and 92/143 indices are supported, but 198 and 89 respectively have no certificate. For example T(1,7) has degree 2log3 and no p=3 certificate, while T(1,16) has degree log7 and no p=7 certificate; the geometric degree is not either ordered or unordered certificate count.
not_done: No independent numerical differentiation of the Siegel series or global compact-Shimura normalisation; these are explicit modular-curve small cases using the cited local identity.
next: Any geometric certificate count must impose the factorisation/ray condition in addition to special-cycle positivity.

summary: Identified the required formal input q^(−cp)e₀ in M^!_{1/2}(ρ_{U⊕<2M>}), M=4cd: it encodes the full Heegner divisor D=−4Mcp, not certificate representatives. For M=4,p=5 I constructed the actual weakly holomorphic input F=(P₅(j−744)−2(j−744))Θ₄ and exactly verified its 20 polar terms; its e₀ principal part is q^−5, but other components add Heegner divisors and poles and its Borcherds weight is 0. The prior memo had an orbit obstruction, not this input calculation; no certificate-specific weakly holomorphic input results.
not_done: No cusp-basis obstruction calculation for the isolated q^−5e₀ term or individual-CM-point divisor construction.
next: A usable input must distinguish certificate points within a Heegner divisor, not merely prescribe its discriminant.
